symptom:
Bun runs the callback of a stdio write inside write(). Node never does. Where should the fix for this live, now that a maintainer's open PR (#45319) already fixes the reported callback order in the sink, and after my own draft PR (#45552) for it turned out to have regressions?

THE BUG ON MAIN (5866b5f13d). process.stdout, process.stderr (pipe, file or TTY), a user-made tty.WriteStream and node:child_process child.stdin are fs.WriteStreams on a FileSink "fast path" (src/js/internal/fs/streams.ts). Their own write() is `writeFast`: it gives each chunk to the FileSink and skips Writable. `fileSink.write(chunk)` returns a number (the sink took the chunk) or a promise (the sink holds it; every write held at that time gets the same promise). writeFast calls `cb(null)` right there when it gets a number (streams.ts:703 on main) and hangs the callback on the promise otherwise.
Repro 1 (main prints 2,1,3 and Node v26.3.0 prints 1,2,3): the parent spawns a child with stdin "pipe" and does `kid.stdin.write(Buffer.alloc((1 << 20) + 1), () => order.push(1)); kid.stdin.write("", () => order.push(2)); kid.stdin.write("x", () => order.push(3)); kid.stdin.end(() => console.log(order.join(",")))`. Script: /tmp/notes-bundle/probes/repro.mjs.
Repro 2: `process.stdout.write(Buffer.alloc(1 << 20)); process.stdout.write("", () => process.exit(0))` into a slow pipe delivers 65536 of 1048576 bytes.
Repro 3: `function next() { process.stdout.write("x", next) } next()` throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. A throw from a callback leaves write(). readline cursor callbacks (process.nextTick) run after later write callbacks.

FACTS VERIFIED ON BUILDS IN THIS CONTAINER.
1. PR #45319 (dylan-conway, maintainer, open since 2026-10-15, git ref origin/pr-45319, +24/-7 in src): FileSink `write_empty`: an empty write() behind a backed-up sink returns the sink's pending promise. Also one 'drain' per promise in streams.ts. On a build of main + #45319, repro 1 prints 1,2,3 and repro 2 delivers all 1048576 bytes. Non-empty chunks written while the sink is backed up already get the promise on main. So #45319 fixes the order while the pipe is full. It leaves the callback inside write() when the sink takes the chunk at once (repro 3).
2. Attempt A = my draft PR oven-sh/bun#45552 (checked out in /workspace/bun, head 87786a6cc). A write that has a callback still gives its chunk to the sink inside write(), and also sends a zero-length marker Buffer through Writable.prototype.write(marker, cb). _write completes the marker at once, or when the "run" of writes parked on one sink promise settles. Writable then orders callbacks with end(), _final, destroy() and cork(). On a contract table (test/js/node/process/process-stdio-write-callback-fixture.js: stream x pipe state idle/parked/failing/broken x call sequence, 111 rows, Node's report is the expected value) A equals Node in 99 rows, main in 33.
   Three self-review rounds found regressions in A each time. Open at its head (release build /tmp/bins/head/bun against main /tmp/bins/main3/bun and node):
   a. `process.stdout.once("error", h); process.stdout.write(big); process.stdout.end()` piped into `head -c 1`: 'error' (EPIPE) is emitted twice, so the process dies of an uncaught EPIPE. Main and Node: once. Cause: two reporters of one sink failure (the run's settle, and the flush promise of _final). A destroys and resets the stream (destroy() + _undestroy()) after the first report, which resets errorEmitted. Probe: /tmp/notes-bundle/probes/round3/headpipe.js once-end.
   b. `Writable.prototype.write.call(process.stdout, "A"); process.stdout.write("B"); process.stdout.write("C\n"); process.exit(0)` prints A. Main and Node: ABC. Cause: A's guard `state.length > 0` in writeFast sends later writes through Writable while Writable holds a chunk, and process.exit() drops Writable's buffer. Probe: round3/window.js.
   c. Stdout is a file: `write("A", w0); Writable.prototype.write.call(out, "B", p1); write("C", w2); end(cb); write("E", w4)`: the end() callback never runs. Main and Node: it gets ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED. Probe: round3/lost-end.js.
   d. A replaced process.stdout._write sees a zero-length chunk per write that has a callback (main: nothing, Node: every chunk).
   e. A needs PR #42031 first (open, red): main drops a tick queued in an 'unhandledRejection' listener, so `process.on("unhandledRejection", e => process.stderr.write(msg, () => process.exit(1)))` exits 0 with any design that defers the callback.
   f. A conflicts with #45319 in src/js/internal/fs/streams.ts.
   Repairs that a reviewer prototyped as binary patches of the release build (round3/mutate2.py, round3/alt.py): the guard `state.length > state.writelen` for b (A's 114 tests still pass), and letting the flush promise of _final and the promise of a real chunk join the run for a.
   A costs, per write that has a callback: 796 ns against 198 ns on main with a new closure per write, 427 against 191 ns with a shared callback (Node 1497 and 496 ns). A write without a callback: no change (130 ns).
3. Attempt B = one line on top of #45319, in writeFast's arm for a chunk the sink took at once: `if (cb !== streamNoop) process.nextTick(cb, null);` in place of `cb(null);`. Local branch scratch/pr45319-tick. Built here: repro 1 prints 1,2,3. B equals Node in 67 of the 111 rows (main + #45319 alone: 44). Where B still differs from Node: every row where the pipe fails (main's order is w0:EPIPE, error, w1:EPIPE and Node's is w0:EPIPE, w1:EPIPE, error), cork() (the callbacks do not wait for uncork()), Writable.prototype.write followed by write() on a child.stdin that is not constructed yet (open PR #45195 makes it born constructed), a throw from the callback of a held write (unhandled rejection, Node: uncaught exception), and how callbacks share ticks. B has the dependency e too.
4. Earlier work: #33484 (robobun, closed by a stale sweep with no maintainer objection): in writeFast, nextTick for an accepted write and chaining onto the parked promise. #33508 removed writeFast: 22 to 24% slower on every write. #43879 recorded that sending writeFast through Writable.prototype.write was considered and not taken. #37128 no longer touches streams.ts.
5. The ask came as an automated note on a maintainer's account: "bring the fix from 33484 back onto main as one PR", and "if the small fix would only get in the way of another PR, say so and leave the choice to the maintainer".

HOW TO RUN THINGS HERE. Do not edit /workspace/bun, do not run `bun bd` there, do not change /tmp/bins.
- node: /usr/local/bin/node (v26.3.0). main: /tmp/bins/main3/bun (release). A: /tmp/bins/head/bun (release, same src as the PR head).
- main + #45319 (debug build): `BUN_DEBUG_QUIET_LOGS=1 /tmp/my-in.sh /tmp/js-pr45319 /tmp/bins/pr45319/bun-debug <args>`. B: the same command with /tmp/js-pr45319-tick. (The debug binary loads the built-in JS from a directory; my-in.sh mounts the given one.)
- One table row: `<runtime> /tmp/c3/fixture-head.js <stdout|stderr|child.stdin> <idle|parked|failing|broken> "<sequence>"`. All rows: `node /tmp/c3/all-rows-c3.mjs <runtime>`. Saved reports: /tmp/tbl2/out3-node.jsonl, out3-main.jsonl, out3-head.jsonl, /tmp/c3/out3-pr45319.jsonl, /tmp/c3/out3-pr45319-tick.jsonl. Compare: `node /tmp/tbl2/cmp2.mjs <a> <b>`.

THE QUESTION. For what #45319 leaves, which shape is right: A repaired, B, a change in the sink, something else, or no change from this side until #45319 and #42031 are in? Count what each shape costs callers who never hit the bug, and name the regressions each one risks.
